notes: 12 upper-division courses plus the undergraduate language requirement. Elective and related-department lists corrected against the live catalog page: the specialization uses a fixed linguistics-elective list and two courses from other departments (not general LIGN).

buckets.label: Undergraduate language requirement (non-English language proficiency)
buckets.note: Proficiency in a non-English natural language; satisfied by coursework or examination. Not a fixed course set. Satisfied one of three ways per the LING-ug catalog page: (1) pass a departmental reading-proficiency exam + oral interview in French, German, Italian, Russian, Spanish, Arabic, Farsi, Tagalog, Portuguese, Vietnamese, or ASL; (2) complete a UCSD course representing the 4th quarter (or beyond) of a single non-English natural language with C- or better; or (3) score 4+ on an AP exam in a non-English language. Terminal course = 4th-quarter language level (e.g. SPAN 20A, etc.).

buckets.label: One introductory course in phonetics, phonology, or morphology
One introductory course in syntax, semantics, or pragmatics
Area distribution: one course from each of two of three areas
buckets.note: One course from each of TWO of the three areas: Computational Linguistics (117, 165, 167, 168, 169); Crosslinguistic Variation (108, 139, 141, 142, 143, 148, 152, 177); Language and Society (105, 146, 174, 175, 176, 177, 178). The Language and Cognition area is the specialization focus, covered by the electives below.

buckets.label: Cognition-and-language linguistics electives
buckets.note: Four linguistics electives from the specialization's approved list on the catalog page. Corrected: prior harvest included LIGN 154 (not on the specialization elective list) and omitted several listed courses.

buckets.label: Additional upper-division courses in related departments
